gaps.note: Edit cuts to Jeff adjusting his ring, hiding his immediate reaction to Kevin's challenge.

stage_a.note: Jeff delivers the pitch with strong, enthusiastic engagement and confident vocal variety.
Sustained engagement and excitement about the product are evident throughout his presentation.
Friendly and approachable demeanor, though largely focused on the business proposition.

venture.description: A digital wallet that allows customers to save their loose change at checkout without downloading an app.
venture.note: The product is a digital system for saving change, pitched as a service for both merchants and consumers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff introduces himself, asks for 250k for 7.5%, and explains how CoinOut digitizes loose change without requiring an app.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks how Jeff plans to survive against giant payment operators without getting crushed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains that cash is still widely used and that their technology and regulatory structure provide a strong defense.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark interrupts to state that nobody believes cash is going away.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff attempts to continue his explanation respectfully.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reiterates his belief that the business will be crushed by competitors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff details the difficulty of building the technology and the required banking and regulatory relationships.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks what incentive a retailer has to install the system.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains that handling cash is expensive for retailers and that the system acts as a loyalty program.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about the barista looking at Jeff with fear.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff asks Kevin to let him finish his point.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff concludes that the system builds a connection between merchants and previously anonymous cash customers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert praises the idea, noting his own dislike for carrying change.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori jokes that Robert hates change because he is rich.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks Jeff to explain the revenue model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states they charge merchants twenty dollars a month.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks for clarification on the monthly fee.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff confirms the fee and adds they earn three percent on each transaction.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff shares his background, including turning down an offer at Apple to pursue this business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori expresses impressed surprise at Jeff's background story.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff continues his story, emphasizing his relentless commitment to the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori asks how much money has been invested in the company so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states they have raised 460k from family, friends, and his own funds.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark points out the difficulty and cost of getting people to use a new application.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff acknowledges Mark's point.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark adds that Jeff is trying to take a share of the merchant's monthly application budget.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff agrees but emphasizes that loose change remains an unsolved problem.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark holds up his credit card as his solution to the problem.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff counters with data showing that a significant portion of transactions are still done in cash.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff elaborates on the value of data and how merchants miss out on cash customers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara compliments Jeff on his ability to handle the sharks' questions confidently.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff thanks Barbara for the compliment.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Jeff to share what is currently working in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff shares that they have processed 2500 transactions in four months with high customer retention.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert notes that the core problem solved is for people who dislike change.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff agrees with Robert's assessment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks to confirm that the system stores the user's phone number in the cloud.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff confirms the mechanism.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark praises the simplicity of using a phone number for a loyalty program.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin criticizes Jeff for focusing solely on the CoinOut feature.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff states his disagreement with Kevin's assessment.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, stating his concern that both consumers and baristas need to be aware of the system.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Mark's decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori exits, noting she doesn't carry cash and is unsure of the investment return.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Lori's decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff shares his vision of reaching 100k locations and a thirty million run rate.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara asks how long it will take to secure a thousand retailers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff projects reaching 700 locations by the end of the year and 3000 the following year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara expresses belief in Jeff's ability to achieve his goals.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara offers 250k for 15 percent, contingent on reaching 700 locations by year end.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff appreciates the offer but states the contingency is untenable.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara questions why he won't accept if he believes his own projections.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff reiterates his refusal to accept a location-based contingency.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara expresses confusion over his reluctance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff explains it is not in his interest to make the deal dependent on those specific projections.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara states she is losing confidence in him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff argues that a strict contingency shows a lack of belief in the broader vision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin interjects that Jeff lacks belief himself.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff denies Kevin's accusation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin insists Jeff would never make a deal like that.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff admits he would consider it if it were his only option.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara shares her own experience of guaranteeing a loan, emphasizing the need for certainty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff acknowledges her perspective.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Barbara exits due to his refusal of the contingency.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts her decision.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin offers 250k for 25 percent, taking more equity for the lack of contingency.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff thanks Kevin and asks if there are any other offers.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin argues the higher equity is the cost of Jeff's lack of confidence.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff tells Kevin he hasn't felt any genuine interest from him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin replies that the deal is about money, not love.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff emphasizes the need for a supportive partner.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert offers 250k for 15 percent, contingent on a successful pilot with a large retailer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff calls the contingency fair and counters with 10 percent equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert clarifies the equity amounts of the standing offers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff counters again, asking if Robert will accept 12.5 percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert refuses to lower his equity requirement.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark advises Jeff to make a decision and move from theory to reality.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff repeats his request for 12.5 percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert firmly maintains his offer at 15 percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff prepares to concede to the 15 percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin laughs at Jeff's joking condition.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jeff accepts Robert's offer of 15 percent with the pilot contingency.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert confirms the deal is done.

decisions.note: Thinks it's a problem that the consumer and barista both need to be aware of it.
Hates coins, doesn't carry money, unsure if it will take off or fizzle.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 15% contingent on getting 700 locations by year end.
decisions.note: Believes he can make it happen but wants a contingency on locations.
Loses confidence because he won't accept the contingency on locations.
Offers a deal without contingency but takes more equity for the risk.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 15% contingent on a successful pilot with a large retailer.
decisions.note: Wants proof of concept with a large retailer before committing fully.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 10% contingent on a successful pilot with a large retailer.
decisions.note: Accepts the contingency but asks for less equity.

decisions.terms: $250,000 for 12.5% contingent on a successful pilot with a large retailer.
decisions.note: Proposes his maximum equity limit of 12.5%.
Accepts the 15% offer with a joking contingency that Kevin can't use it.
